notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch) was sufficient; site is fully server-rendered, no block encountered. robots.txt checked first: no Claude-specific UA disallow (only generic Disallow rules for /downloads/, /system/, /sitecore/, /checkout/, /Json/*, and a testlang query param) — proceeded. Checked: (1) full English (/en) homepage nav/mega-menu — top-level categories are only Furniture, Lighting, Accessories, News, Product Collections, About/Journal/Professionals; Accessories expands to Kitchen, Tableware, Candleholders, Organizing (Stationery, Hooks & Shoehorns), Objects, Vases, Mirrors — no holiday-named node anywhere. (2) Full Danish (/da) homepage nav — structurally identical, same node names transliterated, no 'jul' (Christmas), 'påske' (Easter), 'halloween', 'advent', or 'nytår' (New Year) node. (3) /en/products/news page — this is a 'new arrivals' listing, not a seasonal/holiday category (title 'News', generic new-product grid, no holiday framing). (4) /en/product/product-collections page — named design collections (e.g. Timb, Puff), no holiday-themed collection. (5) Internal site search for 'christmas' on /en/search — 0 hits (data-totalhits="0"). (6) Internal site search for 'jul' on /da/search — returned totalhits=7, but inspection of the actual result items showed these are false-positive substring matches on 'hjul' (Danish for 'wheel', e.g. 'Form drejestol m. 4 hjul alu' = swivel chair with 4 wheels), not Christmas products — confirms no Christmas-tagged products exist, not merely that the term is absent from titles. (7) robots.txt has no sitemap.xml directive and https://www.normann-copenhagen.com/sitemap.xml returned HTTP 500, so sitemap enumeration was not available; nav + search + collections page were used as the taxonomy-discovery method instead, per the site's own structure (no CMS-driven seasonal landing pages found via any route). (8) Accessories category page's marketing copy mentions 'seasons' generically ('Each season inspires us... summery feel... winter coziness') but this is decorative brand copy about a normal Accessories category, not a genuine holiday-specific PLP, so it was excluded per the boundary rule against categories that merely contain/reference seasonal products. No genuine Christmas, Halloween, Easter, Diwali, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, or other holiday/festival category, sub-category, or collection exists anywhere in Normann Copenhagen's taxonomy in either language. Conclusion: no_seasonal, rows empty.
